# Curated Web3 Testing Resources

Quality over quantity. Every resource listed here has been personally vetted for accuracy, usefulness, and current relevance. This is your go-to reference for expanding your Web3 testing knowledge beyond what's covered on this site.

---

## 🛠️ Essential Development Frameworks

### **Hardhat**
- **Official Documentation**: [hardhat.org](https://hardhat.org/) — The gold standard for Ethereum development and testing
- **Testing Guide**: [hardhat.org/tutorial/testing-contracts](https://hardhat.org/tutorial/testing-contracts.html) — Comprehensive testing walkthrough
- **Network Forking**: [hardhat.org/hardhat-network/guides/mainnet-forking](https://hardhat.org/hardhat-network/guides/mainnet-forking.html) — Test against real mainnet state

### **Foundry**
- **Official Book**: [book.getfoundry.sh](https://book.getfoundry.sh/) — Complete Foundry documentation and tutorials
- **Testing Framework**: [book.getfoundry.sh/forge/tests](https://book.getfoundry.sh/forge/tests) — Forge testing capabilities
- **Fuzzing Guide**: [book.getfoundry.sh/forge/fuzz-testing](https://book.getfoundry.sh/forge/fuzz-testing) — Property-based testing with Foundry

### **Brownie**
- **Documentation**: [eth-brownie.readthedocs.io](https://eth-brownie.readthedocs.io/) — Python-based smart contract testing
- **Testing Guide**: [eth-brownie.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tests.html](https://eth-brownie.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tests.html) — Python testing patterns

---

## 🔍 Static Analysis & Security Tools

### **Slither**
- **GitHub Repository**: [github.com/crytic/slither](https://github.com/crytic/slither) — Leading static analysis tool for Solidity
- **Detector Documentation**: [github.com/crytic/slither/wiki/Detector-Documentation](https://github.com/crytic/slither/wiki/Detector-Documentation) — Complete list of vulnerabilities it catches
- **Integration Guide**: [github.com/crytic/slither/wiki/Usage](https://github.com/crytic/slither/wiki/Usage) — How to integrate into your workflow

### **Mythril**
- **Official Documentation**: [mythril-classic.readthedocs.io](https://mythril-classic.readthedocs.io/) — Security analysis platform
- **Detection Modules**: [mythril-classic.readthedocs.io/en/master/analysis-modules.html](https://mythril-classic.readthedocs.io/en/master/analysis-modules.html) — Understanding what it detects

### **Echidna**
- **GitHub Repository**: [github.com/crytic/echidna](https://github.com/crytic/echidna) — Property-based fuzzing for smart contracts
- **Tutorial Series**: [secure-contracts.com/program-analysis/echidna/introduction/](https://secure-contracts.com/program-analysis/echidna/introduction/) — Hands-on Echidna learning

---

## 🌐 End-to-End Testing

### **Playwright**
- **Official Documentation**: [playwright.dev](https://playwright.dev/) — Modern web testing framework
- **Web3 Integration**: [playwright.dev/docs/test-runners](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-runners) — Using Playwright with Web3 applications

### **Cypress**
- **Documentation**: [docs.cypress.io](https://docs.cypress.io/) — Popular E2E testing framework
- **dApp Testing Patterns**: [docs.cypress.io/guides/end-to-end-testing/testing-strategies](https://docs.cypress.io/guides/end-to-end-testing/testing-strategies) — Strategies for testing decentralized apps

---

## 📚 Security & Best Practices

### **OpenZeppelin**
- **Contracts Documentation**: [docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts](https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts/) — Battle-tested smart contract components
- **Security Guidelines**: [docs.openzeppelin.com/learn/preparing-for-mainnet](https://docs.openzeppelin.com/learn/preparing-for-mainnet) — Pre-deployment security checklist
- **Test Helpers**: [docs.openzeppelin.com/test-helpers](https://docs.openzeppelin.com/test-helpers/) — Utilities for testing smart contracts

### **ConsenSys Security Best Practices**
- **Smart Contract Best Practices**: [consensys.github.io/smart-contract-best-practices](https://consensys.github.io/smart-contract-best-practices/) — Comprehensive security guide
- **Known Attacks**: [consensys.github.io/smart-contract-best-practices/attacks](https://consensys.github.io/smart-contract-best-practices/attacks/) — Common vulnerability patterns

### **Trail of Bits Resources**
- **Building Secure Contracts**: [github.com/crytic/building-secure-contracts](https://github.com/crytic/building-secure-contracts) — Security-focused development guide
- **Awesome Ethereum Security**: [github.com/crytic/awesome-ethereum-security](https://github.com/crytic/awesome-ethereum-security) — Curated security resources

---

## 🔧 Developer Tools & Utilities

### **eth-gas-reporter**
- **GitHub Repository**: [github.com/cgewecke/eth-gas-reporter](https://github.com/cgewecke/eth-gas-reporter) — Gas usage reporting for tests
- **Integration Examples**: Gas optimization testing patterns

### **solidity-coverage**
- **GitHub Repository**: [github.com/sc-forks/solidity-coverage](https://github.com/sc-forks/solidity-coverage) — Code coverage for Solidity testing
- **Configuration Guide**: Setting up coverage reporting

### **Tenderly**
- **Documentation**: [docs.tenderly.co](https://docs.tenderly.co/) — Debugging and monitoring platform
- **Simulation API**: [docs.tenderly.co/simulations-and-forks](https://docs.tenderly.co/simulations-and-forks) — Testing with transaction simulations

---

## 📖 Learning Resources

### **Official Documentation**
- **Ethereum Development**: [ethereum.org/developers](https://ethereum.org/developers/) — Official Ethereum developer resources
- **Solidity Documentation**: [docs.soliditylang.org](https://docs.soliditylang.org/) — Complete Solidity language reference
- **Web3.js Documentation**: [web3js.readthedocs.io](https://web3js.readthedocs.io/) — JavaScript library for Ethereum

### **Educational Platforms**
- **Ethereum.org Tutorials**: [ethereum.org/developers/tutorials](https://ethereum.org/developers/tutorials/) — Step-by-step development guides
- **CryptoZombies**: [cryptozombies.io](https://cryptozombies.io/) — Interactive smart contract development course
- **Buildspace**: [buildspace.so](https://buildspace.so/) — Project-based Web3 learning

### **Community Resources**
- **Ethereum Stack Exchange**: [ethereum.stackexchange.com](https://ethereum.stackexchange.com/) — Q&A for Ethereum developers
- **OpenZeppelin Forum**: [forum.openzeppelin.com](https://forum.openzeppelin.com/) — Smart contract development discussions
- **Ethereum Research**: [ethresear.ch](https://ethresear.ch/) — Cutting-edge Ethereum research and discussions

---

## 🧪 Testing-Specific Resources

### **Testing Patterns & Strategies**
- **Smart Contract Testing Best Practices**: Key patterns for comprehensive test coverage
- **Gas Optimization Testing**: Strategies for testing gas efficiency
- **Security Testing Methodologies**: Systematic approaches to security validation

### **Mock & Test Data**
- **Test Data Generation**: Tools and patterns for creating realistic test scenarios
- **Mock Contract Patterns**: Strategies for testing contract interactions
- **Fixture Management**: Organizing and maintaining test data

---

## 🔗 Community & Updates

### **Stay Current**
- **Week in Ethereum News**: [weekinethereumnews.com](https://weekinethereumnews.com/) — Weekly Ethereum ecosystem updates
- **Ethereum Improvement Proposals**: [eips.ethereum.org](https://eips.ethereum.org/) — Official EIP repository
- **Web3 Security Database**: [github.com/rekt-research/rekt-database](https://github.com/rekt-research/rekt-database) — Learn from past security incidents

### **Professional Networks**
- **Ethereum Developers**: Twitter, LinkedIn, and Discord communities
- **Security Researchers**: Follow leading security firms and researchers
- **Testing Communities**: Join testing-focused Web3 communities

---

## 💡 Pro Tips

**🎯 Start Here**: If you're new to Web3 testing, begin with Hardhat's official testing guide, then move to OpenZeppelin's security guidelines.

**🔄 Stay Updated**: Web3 moves fast. Follow the official Twitter accounts of your primary tools for breaking changes and new features.

**🤝 Community First**: When stuck, the Ethereum Stack Exchange and OpenZeppelin Forum are goldmines for practical solutions.

**🔐 Security Mindset**: Always cross-reference security practices with multiple sources. What worked yesterday might be vulnerable today.

---
